# Compatibility

<!-- Generated by fixtures/tools/compat.py; edit only between the hand-written markers. -->

What surimono does and doesn't do yet, from test results. Every known failure is listed with the test that proves it. Expectations come from Chrome, specs and WPT, and are never edited to match surimono's output.

Results: fixtures from 99c363cd359c281c34bf99e6de0337f3bf569ac8 (surimono CLI surimono 0.0.0, sha256 7c8d26582fbe, commit 99c363cd359c281c34bf99e6de0337f3bf569ac8); hostile scripts from their results file; benchmark from bench/run.sh.

### Speed and memory against Grover

From `bench/run.sh` on GitHub Actions, commit 15b530e02, 20 runs; Chromium Google Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12, grover 1.2.10, fulgur 0.40.0. Medians; peak memory is summed PSS over the process tree. The full table is in `bench/results/15b530e0/summary.md`.

| System | Cold | Warm | Peak memory, cold | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grover (Chrome) | 1,698 ms | 1,268 ms | 589 MB | measured |
| surimono + fulgur (Ruby) | 694 ms | 538 ms | 101 MB | measured |
| surimono + fulgur (Rust) | 570 ms | 538 ms | 74 MB | measured |
| fulgur only, Chrome's SVGs (reference point) | 245 ms | 118 ms | 68 MB | reference point, not surimono |
| Grover (chrome-headless-shell) | 1,284 ms | 1,009 ms | 383 MB | measured |
| Grover, new Chrome per document | — | 1,534 ms | — | measured |

Memory target (`docs/SPEC.md`): at least 5× lower peak (summed PSS) than Grover, set by Kay at checkpoint 2 (4 Nov 2026, down from 10×). Measured, cold: 5.8× Ruby and 8.0× Rust. fulgur alone, with no JavaScript, reaches 8.7×, which is why the target isn't higher: it is expected to bound surimono's ratio, not a proven bound. Against Grover on chrome-headless-shell, the leanest Chrome it can run: 3.8× Ruby and 5.2× Rust.

## Known gaps

| Gap | Evidence | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `toLocaleString`, `toLocaleDateString` and the other `toLocale*String` methods ignore the locale argument in the sandbox (QuickJS has no Intl data): `new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1)).toLocaleDateString("ja-JP")` gives `"1/1/2026"`; Chrome gives `"2026/1/1"` | Reported by the reviewer of the core sandbox (p1-rt-05); Chrome's output checked in Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (time zone UTC): `"2026/1/1"`, `"2026/1/1 0:00:00"` for `toLocaleString("ja-JP")`, and `"1.234.567,5"` for `(1234567.5).toLocaleString("de-DE")` | Japanese (or any non-US) chart labels that format dates or numbers through `toLocale*String` come out in US format. The checkpoint-2 fixtures format through ECharts and Vega format strings instead, so they don't hit it |
| Vega and Vega-Lite islands load no images or links: an `image` mark or an `href` channel (http or `data:` URL, Vega or Vega-Lite) fails the island with a refusal that names the URL: `surimono: islands have no network or file access, so Vega image marks are not supported; this spec loads the image "…"`, or `surimono: Vega links (href) are not supported in islands; this spec links "…"`. There is no network by design, so data must be inline (`values`) | Review of #29 (P1-RT-07): all of these render in Chrome. The refusal is from P1-RT-12 (#39): `noLoader` in `crates/islands/js/src/vega.js`, pinned in `crates/islands/tests/vega.rs` for Vega and Vega-Lite, http and `data:` | A chart with images or clickable marks fails as a whole. Data loaded by `url` is refused as well; inline it with `values` |
| A Vega-Lite `"width": "container"` (or `"height": "container"`) renders at 300×300, not at the island's `data-width` and `data-height` | Review of #29 (P1-RT-07). Vega-Lite 6.5.0 compiles `"container"` to `isFinite(containerSize()[0]) ? containerSize()[0] : <config.view.continuousWidth>` (`src/compile/layoutsize/assemble.ts`; the default is 300), and a headless View has no container element to measure | Responsive Vega-Lite specs come out at the default size; give the island spec fixed `width` and `height` (or set `config.view.continuousWidth` and `continuousHeight` to the island's size) |
| Island text printed as outlines (`TextMode::Outlines`, the default) doesn't support `rotate`, `textLength`, `<textPath>` (its content is dropped), vertical writing modes, `word-spacing`, `baseline-shift`, text decoration, synthetic bold, font properties set only by `<style>` rules, or fonts inherited from the page outside the SVG (the defaults are 16px and `serif`). The text keeps its position on a straight baseline | `crates/gfx/src/svg/text.rs` module docs (P1-GFX-05, #27); its layout is otherwise checked character by character against Chromium 153 (`crates/gfx/tests/chrome/svg_text.mjs`, `tests/data/chrome_svg_text.json`) | Rotated axis labels, underlined or path-following text and `<style>`-only font rules print differently from Chrome. ECharts and Vega set fonts as attributes and don't use these features in the checkpoint-2 fixtures |
| `Math.sin`, `Math.exp`, `Math.pow` and their kin come from the platform's C library, which can differ in the last bit between glibc, musl and macOS | `crates/core/src/sandbox.rs` docs (P1-RT-02) | Output is byte-identical across runs on one platform (the determinism rule); across platforms, SVG coordinates computed with those functions can differ in their last digits. Seen on macOS: one ulp in a d3 centroid. On x86_64 Linux `d3-charts` equals Chrome's DOM exactly; `crates/dom/tests/real_world.rs` compares fractions to 1e-9 relative on every other platform (#144) |
| `Number.prototype.toLocaleString` has no digit grouping in the sandbox: `(1234567.891).toLocaleString()` gives `"1234567.891"`; Chrome gives `"1,234,567.891"` (and the same for `"ja-JP"`) | quickjs-ng 0.16.2 (rquickjs-sys 0.14.0, `quickjs/quickjs.c`) defines `Number.prototype.toLocaleString` as `JS_CFUNC_MAGIC_DEF("toLocaleString", 0, js_number_toString, 1)`: `toString` in base 10, no grouping; the sandbox prelude (`crates/core/src/prelude.js`) replaces only `Date`'s `toLocale*` methods. A sandbox test asserting `"1234567.891"` is requested from the runtime engineer. Chrome's checked in Chromium 153.0.8010.12 (locale en-US, time zone UTC): `"1,234,567.891"` for both calls, `"0.5"` for `(0.5).toLocaleString()` | Axis labels and tooltips that format numbers through `toLocaleString` lose their thousands separators. ECharts 6.1.0 never calls it (its bundle has no `toLocaleString`); Vega 6.4.0's d3-format calls `toLocaleString("en")` only for `d` formats of 1e21 or more, and strips the commas |
| `TextMode::Keep` (island text left as `<text>`) is an expected failure with fulgur 0.40: fulgur prints that text in system fonts, or not at all, never in the fonts registered with it (see "Inline SVG text prints in system fonts" under the fulgur gaps below) | `crates/gfx/tests/fulgur_print.rs` (P1-GFX-05) asserts the failure still happens, so a fixed fulgur or Blitz shows up there | That is why `TextMode::Outlines` is the default. Use Keep only with a PDF engine that sets inline SVG text in the registered fonts |
| vegalite-line-ja's island, printed by fulgur, fails the shape check by 0.2 points: 10.2% (limit 10%) in the 32×32 window at 240,288, which holds the 10 px x-axis label "6月". The same SVG printed by Chrome passes (4.8%), and fulgur printing Chrome's SVG with real text scores 0.0% there. The glyphs are in place; their anti-aliasing differs: outlined text is a filled PDF path, Chrome's reference is font text | Checkpoint-2 runs from 6eb38139 (P1-CF-09) and 99c363cd (P1-CF-13), with the same scores (`fixtures/checkpoint-2/vegalite-line-ja/island-0-fulgur/`, side by side with `island-0-chrome/`) | Small CJK labels print a little differently from Chrome at 96 dpi; the page comparison of the same fixture passes (7.3%, fulgur's floor 1.3%). Not a checkpoint-2 gate failure (the gate is the Chrome-printed island) |
| `Date.parse` of a non-ISO string follows QuickJS, not V8: it accepts the zone names CET, CEST, WET, WEST, EET and EEST, and negative years. `Date.parse('Jan 1 2026 10:00 CET')` and `'Sep 13 275760 01:00 CEST'` give a time; Chromium 153.0.8010.12 gives `NaN` for those zones and for `'Apr 19 -271821 23:00 EST'`, and agrees on `PST` | `crates/core/src/prelude.js`, "Date.parse": a port of quickjs-ng's parser, so no string depends on the host's zone. ECMA-262 §21.4.3.2 leaves non-ISO formats to the implementation, so neither answer breaks the spec. Chrome's checked with `Date.parse` in that build | A script that parses those strings gets a date where Chrome gets an invalid one. Rare, since ISO strings behave the same everywhere |
| `Document::to_html` starts at `<html>`, so serialized HTML has no doctype, and a reparse would be in quirks mode unless the caller adds one. The tree has the doctype: `document.doctype` and `document.firstChild` answer as in Chromium 153.0.8010.12 | `wpt/probes`, `doctype`. `crates/dom/DESIGN.md`, "Several documents" | Only output that is parsed again |
| `Attr` is a partial `Node`: `nodeType`, `nodeName`, `nodeValue`, `textContent`, `parentNode`, `ownerDocument`, `baseURI` and `ownerElement` answer, but `firstChild`, `childNodes`, `isConnected`, `cloneNode` and `getRootNode` throw a `TypeError`, "the member isn't available on this object". In Chromium 153.0.8010.12 `Attr` is a full `Node` | `wpt/probes`, `attr`. `Document::node_of` in `crates/dom/src/host.rs`, `crates/dom/tests/collections.rs`, `attributes_map`. DOM §4.9.2 | A script that calls a tree method on an `Attr` stops with an exception. Rare outside WPT |
| `while (…) await sleep(0)` never moves the virtual clock, and ends in `TaskLimit`. A timer set from a microtask starts at nesting level 0, so the 4 ms clamp never applies; with `var ready = false; setTimeout(() => ready = true, 100);` the flag is never set. Chromium 153.0.8010.12 keeps the level through microtasks and clamps from the seventh round, so the same loop ends. The spec wins for DOM behaviour | HTML, timer initialization steps: the level comes from the currently running task, and a microtask checkpoint makes the microtask that task. Pinned by `awaiting_a_zero_timer_does_not_move_the_clock` in `crates/core/tests/event_loop.rs`. Chrome's delays in ms (#99, fresh page per case, 3 runs): `await sleep(0)` 0.1 0 0 0 0 0 4.4 4.2 4.2; `setTimeout` from `queueMicrotask` 0 0 0 0 0 4.4 4.3 4.3; from `then` 0 0 0 0 0 4.2 4.3 4.2; a nested `setTimeout`, the control, 0 0 0 0 0 4.3 4.2 4.3, which matches surimono | A page that polls with `await sleep(0)` for something a later timer sets stops at the task limit, with the timer not run. Polling with a non-zero delay, or a plain nested `setTimeout`, moves the clock as in Chrome |
| A NUL inside a string literal or a comment of a string handler (`setTimeout("log.push('a\0b'.length)")`, with a real NUL in the source) is reported as a `SyntaxError`, and the handler doesn't run. It is valid source: `SourceCharacter` in ECMA-262 (Source Text) is any code point, `eval` in the sandbox gives 3, and so does the handler in Chromium 153.0.8010.12. A NUL outside a literal is a `SyntaxError` everywhere | String handlers reach the parser as a C string (`Ctx::eval_raw` is private in rquickjs). Pinned by `nul_and_lone_surrogates_in_string_handlers` in `crates/core/tests/event_loop.rs`. Chrome's checked in that build with the test's own handlers: 3, and one `SyntaxError` for the NUL outside a literal | The page goes on and the error is in the settle report (`uncaught`), but that one handler does nothing. Rare: a string handler is legacy, and a NUL in one rarer |
| A lone surrogate in a string handler reads as U+FFFD: `setTimeout("log.push('\ud800'.charCodeAt(0))")`, with a real lone surrogate in the source, gives 65533. `eval` in the sandbox and the handler in Chromium 153.0.8010.12 give 55296 | The handler's source reaches the parser as UTF-8, which can't hold a surrogate. Same test as the row above; Chrome's checked in that build | Only string handlers that hold unpaired surrogates in the source text. |
| `location` doesn't exist on the window: `typeof location` is `undefined`, and `location.href` a `ReferenceError`, in Chromium 153.0.8010.12 an object. `parent`, `top` and `opener` answer. `document.URL` is `about:blank` unless the caller gives a URL. The WPT runner defines `location` at the start of `testharness.js`'s script, as plain data, so its rates don't depend on this gap and don't measure it either | `wpt/probes`, `location`, `stalerows`. `wpt/runner/src/main.rs`, `ENVIRONMENT`; `wpt/README.md`, "Harness environment". HTML, `Location` | A page or library that reads `location` stops with an exception |
| The WPT denominator is smaller than wpt.fyi's, and for dom/events by a lot: the Chrome baseline runs on a static server, not wptserve, so subtests that need its Python handlers, or a real browser's input and scrolling, aren't in it. A subtest we fail there can't lower a rate | `wpt/README.md`, "Baseline" and "Which tests can't run". Chrome's passes in the baseline against wpt.fyi's Chrome 156 run at the same commit: dom/nodes 15267 of 15300, dom/events 748 of 848, domparsing 909 of 913, timers and microtasks 34 of 34. The rates on both counts are in the table above | dom/events's baseline is 100 subtests short, 11.8%, so its rate is the most flattered: 524 passes would meet 70% of 748 and be 61.8% of 848. Report dom/events on both denominators against its target. The other areas differ by under 1% |

The DOM keeps the lone code unit (56832, 55296), since a DOM string is UTF-16 code units; `length` and offsets are right | `crates/dom/src/tree.rs`, `crates/dom/DESIGN.md`, "Half a surrogate pair". ## Where the spec and Chromium disagree

Every row is a conflict the fleet rule settles: the spec wins for DOM behaviour, so surimono follows the spec and differs from Chromium 153.0.8010.12. None of them changes how a page prints. `wpt/probes` reruns each one in both. One more spec-against-Chromium conflict is settled the same way but can change what a page does, so it sits in Known gaps: `while (…) await sleep(0)`.

| Behaviour | Spec, and surimono | Chromium 153 | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `!important` in a `style` attribute: where a declaration stays | CSSOM keeps source order: `height: 1px; color: red !important; width: 1px` reads back unchanged | Sometimes moves it after the normal ones: `height: 1px; width: 1px; color: red !important;`, yet keeps `color: red !important; width: 1px;` | `crates/dom/src/style_attr.rs`, `important_keeps_source_order`; review of #97 |
| `style` attribute order in the serialized tag, when a script sets `element.style` and then another attribute | CSSOM §6.6 updates the attribute at once, so `style` comes first | Adds it lazily, when something reads the attributes, so it serializes last | `crates/dom/tests/real_world.rs`, `style_last`, which moves `style` to the end of each tag on both sides of the comparison (#104) |
| `normalize()` on a lone text node | DOM §4.4 step 4, "replace data" (§4.10 step 4): one `characterData` record, with the old value | No record | `crates/dom/tests/observers.rs`, `normalize_queues_its_records_in_tree_order`; review of #105 |
| `normalize()` merging several text nodes | One `characterData` record, then all the removals | One `characterData` and one removal per merged node, and an empty member of the run is removed before merging | Same test and review |
| `previousSibling` in the record of `a.replaceChild(p, q)`, where `p` was `q`'s previous sibling | §4.2.3 reads it before adopting, so the record has `p` | Null | Review of #105. Probed on main 89343c8f |
| `outerHTML` with text at the edge of the new content, beside a text node | DOM Parsing has no merge step: one record, adding the element and the text | Merges the text edge with the next text node: `add[B,"2z"]`, then a `characterData` and a removal | Review of #105. Probed on main 89343c8f |
| `splitText` record order | §4.11: insert first, then replace data | `characterData` first | Review of #105. Probed on main 89343c8f |
| `[a="b" s]`, the case-sensitive flag | Selectors 4 defines `s`, and it matches here | `SyntaxError` | `wpt/probes`, `selectors` |
| `HTMLDocument` | HTML §7.2.2: `window.HTMLDocument` is the `Document` interface object, so `HTMLDocument === Document`, and `document.constructor.name` is `Document` | A separate interface: `HTMLDocument === Document` is false, and the name is `HTMLDocument` | `wpt/probes`, `htmldoc`. `crates/dom/tests/nodes.rs` (#131). 20 subtests of `dom/events/passive-by-default.html` put that name in their own names, `… for HTMLDocument`, so ours report `… for Document` and they count as lost |
| `label.control` with `for`, on a label not in a document | HTML §4.10.4 looks "in the tree", so a detached label finds the control beside it or inside it, and `click()` reaches it | Null, and the click goes nowhere: it looks only in the document | `wpt/probes`, `label`. Review of #135; `a_labels_control_ignores_hidden_inputs_and_stays_in_its_tree` in `crates/dom/tests/events.rs` |
| A handler that returns `false` on a non-cancelable event | HTML §8.1.7.1 sets the canceled flag, whether or not the event can be canceled, so `dispatchEvent` returns `false` | `dispatchEvent` returns `true` | Review of #104; `crates/dom/src/glue_events.js`. Probed on main 89343c8f: `false`, `defaultPrevented` true |

## Printing gaps in fulgur 0.40.0 seen by the fixtures

These are fulgur's (or Blitz's), not surimono's. The fixture page template avoids
them so page diffs measure the islands (fixtures/README.md). Repros were made with
`fulgur render` and inspected in the PDF content stream.

| Gap | Repro | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| A single-side border ignores its colour and prints in `currentColor`: `border-bottom: 1px solid #d0d7de` (or with `border-bottom-color`) prints black on black text; `border: 1px solid #d0d7de` on all sides prints the right colour | `<div style="border-bottom: 2px solid red; height: 10px">` strokes `0 0 0 RG` | Table row rules and header underlines print black instead of light grey |
| A right-aligned flex item wraps earlier than in Chrome | `header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: flex-end }` with a bold 12pt left item and a 9pt right item of three `<br>`-separated lines: fulgur wraps "Revenue report" onto two lines | Everything below moves down by a line, so the whole-page diff fails |
| Table column widths differ from Chrome's, with or without `table-layout: fixed` and `<col style="width: …">` | A 100%-wide table of 3 or 4 columns with right-aligned numbers: fulgur's numeric columns sit tens of pixels from Chrome's; a header that wraps in one engine does not in the other | Every row of the table differs |
| Fractional line heights accumulate differently | `font-size: 10pt; line-height: 1.4` plus mm margins above a chart: the chart lands about 1 px lower in fulgur | Thin chart lines (axes) fall on another pixel row |
| Line boxes do not grow for fallback glyphs | Latin-first font list (`"Noto Sans", "Noto Sans JP"`) on a paragraph containing Japanese: Chrome's line box takes Noto Sans JP's taller metrics, fulgur's does not | Content below moves by a pixel or more |
| No `text-spacing-trim` | Chrome (since 123) trims the spacing between adjacent full-width punctuation such as "）、" by default; fulgur prints full widths | Japanese captions and labels with that punctuation run longer in fulgur |
| SVG text: per-glyph fallback picks the Bold face | An SVG `<text font-family="Noto Sans, Noto Sans JP">10月</text>` (normal weight) with both Noto Sans JP faces available: `pdffonts` on fulgur's PDF of vegalite-layered-dense-ja's island lists only NotoSans-Regular and **NotoSansJP-Bold**; Chrome's lists NotoSansJP-Regular for the same labels. Same in echarts-mixed-dense-ja. When the family list names Noto Sans JP first (vegalite-line-ja), fulgur picks Regular | Japanese glyphs reached through fallback print heavier. This is the remaining fulgur floor on the fixtures: 4.5% (page) and 3.9% (island) on vegalite-layered-dense-ja, 2.5% and 2.9% on echarts-mixed-dense-ja, all within the 10% gate |
| Inline SVG text prints in system fonts: fulgur 0.40 draws inline `<svg>` through blitz-dom 0.2.4's usvg with a font database of system fonts only (`util.rs`), so `<text>` ignores the fonts registered with fulgur | `crates/gfx/tests/fulgur_print.rs` (P1-GFX-05): with `TextMode::Keep`, `pdffonts` on fulgur's PDF lists a system font, or no font, for the island's text, while the HTML text next to it uses the registered fonts; the test asserts this still happens so a fixed fulgur or Blitz shows up | surimono converts island text to vector outlines in the registered fonts by default (`TextMode::Outlines`), so the PDF prints what was measured. The cost: chart labels aren't selectable or searchable text in the PDF (the outline keeps the string as `aria-label`). The fixtures' fulgur baseline prints Chrome's SVGs with only `fixtures/fonts` visible to fontconfig, so it doesn't show this. In the checkpoint-2 runs from 6eb38139 (P1-CF-09) and 99c363cd (`fixtures/checkpoint-2/`, P1-CF-13), `pdffonts` lists no font at all in any of the 12 fulgur-printed island PDFs (all island text is outlines), and only the registered Noto Sans and Noto Sans JP faces in the 11 page PDFs |

## Printing differences in Chrome seen by the fixtures

| Difference | Repro | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Chrome's PDF output drops `fill-opacity` on gradient fills | ECharts' area under a line (`areaStyle` with a linear gradient and its default opacity 0.7) is drawn as `<path fill="url(#zr1-g0)" fill-opacity="0.7">`. Chromium 153 applies the 0.7 on screen: a screenshot gives (240, 187, 153) at one point. Its printed PDF ignores it: (233, 159, 110) at the same point. fulgur prints (239, 187, 153), which agrees with the screen and with the SVG spec (`fill-opacity` applies to paint servers) | A semi-transparent gradient prints darker in Chrome's references than in fulgur or on screen. Spec and Chrome's own screen agree, so the fixtures avoid the case instead of taking a side: echarts-two-charts-latin sets the area's opacity to 1 |
| Chrome rounds `@page` sizes to 1/300 inch | An island page with `@page { size: 640px 340px }`: `pdfinfo` on Chrome's PDF gives 255.12 pt tall instead of 255 pt (380 px gives 285.12 pt). pdftoppm at 96 dpi then rasterises 341 rows where fulgur's exact 255 pt gives 340 | Page sizes differ by one row and the comparison fails on size alone. The fixtures use island sizes in multiples of 8 px (1/12 inch), which are exact; `gen-islands.mjs` refuses others |
| Chrome positions SVG text in 1/64 px layout units and rounds each advance to them | `crates/gfx/src/svg/text.rs` (P1-GFX-05), `layout_matches_chrome`: surimono's outlines use Parley's exact advances (equal to `measureText`'s to 0.0007 px), so each glyph lands up to 1/128 px per preceding character from Chrome's, at most 0.049 px on the reference strings | Far below the fixture comparison's 1 px tolerance; recorded so nobody chases it |
